chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Warwick Hall flops against the new Savoy ballroom
summary: The six-piece band with Louis, Hines and Lil as agent did no business at the old Warwick Hall, while the new Savoy on South Parkway drew the crowds; a jealous husband once pulled a pistol on the band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well this little venture of yours at the Warwick, I mean was that a big band you took in there?

No, it was about six pieces. You see, but we had such big names then. Oh, Father Hines and Louis Armstrong and Lil was our agent you know. She was booking us around and thats when I played over on the West Side. And some cat come in boy and some girl was right in front of the band just shaking and going on. And her old man must have walked in. And he slapped her and come up with pistol, see, and asked Louis, say, what's the matter, you don't like it? And Louis said, man, that's alright with me.
This cat slapped this girl and come up with this big pistol and asked Louis did he like it or not? And Louis said, that's alright with me. But we wasn't
Why do you think that was?
Because I think why it was because the Savoy was a beautiful brand new ballroom. Beautifully decorated, just built you know. It had everything. And the Warwick was an old beat up barn.
Beautiful. I. J. Spagen had it then and the Warwick was........

And they would walk up on to the ballroom when they got there. And gee, nobody is going to go for a beautiful new place. Very modern and fashipnable. I went up there one night with Lill and I think there were six people in the place. (LAUGHTER). Oh, it was sad. (LAUGHTER). Oh it was sad.
Yes, that was a floperoo boy, talk about a floperoo.
